title: From Bloemfontein to Namibia: meet the Boostech network
summary: Your Free State connection to Boostech Namibia, the Western Cape, Johannesburg and the teams in Australia and New Zealand.
image_alt: Toyota Hilux in the Boostech Bloemfontein workshop
context: A regional introduction from Boostech Bloemfontein, with workshop photos shared by the Boostech network.
body:
A local tuning enquiry in Bloemfontein can be the start of a much wider conversation. The Boostech name connects teams across Southern Africa and beyond, with regional websites that let you see the services, projects and people behind the brand.

For Free State drivers, the useful part of that reach is being able to start with a local team while exploring how similar vehicles are used elsewhere. A Hilux working in Namibia, a Ranger towing in the Western Cape and a daily driver in Bloemfontein may share a platform, but the right recommendation still starts with the individual vehicle.

Our Namibia connection

Boostech Namibia is a direct point of contact for drivers in Namibia, with Swakopmund service, Windhoek partner support and countrywide arrangements. Its website brings together ECU remapping, exhaust options and practical vehicle guides.

Namibian use puts the focus on everyday needs: long distances, towing, touring and usable response under load. Explore the Namibia ECU remapping guide and Namibia articles and advice for examples of the questions worth asking before an upgrade. If you are travelling there, contact the Namibia team in advance to discuss your route and what can be arranged.

Western Cape: software and exhaust options

Boostech Western Cape connects the network to Cape Town, with a Durbanville base and mobile support across the city. Work elsewhere in the Western Cape is arranged individually.

Its website covers vehicle-specific software tuning alongside De Graaf and 1-Exhaust options. That makes it a useful resource when considering software and hardware together. Bloemfontein customers should use our local enquiry form to confirm the right application, local availability and fitment arrangements.

Johannesburg and the wider South African network

Boostech Johannesburg adds a Gauteng connection, with its website presenting tuning, exhaust systems and vehicle accessories. Customers spending time in Gauteng can explore those services and contact the local team about their vehicle.

The main Boostech SA website provides a broader introduction to the brand and its dealer network. Together, these regional sites show a business with a presence beyond any one workshop.

Australia and New Zealand

The same name appears across the Indian Ocean. Boostech AUS presents ECU remapping for 4WDs and cars in Perth, while Boostech New Zealand presents tuning, servicing and diagnostics in Auckland.

Familiar platforms such as the Hilux, Ranger and Land Cruiser help make these international projects relevant to Southern African enthusiasts. A build overseas is useful context; the available calibration and hardware for your own vehicle still depend on its exact specification.

Follow the regional teams

The workshops and vehicles shared by the different teams give the Boostech network a face. Explore Boostech Namibia, Boostech Western Cape, Boostech Bloemfontein, Boostech Johannesburg, Boostech SA and Boostech Australia on Instagram.

Start with Bloemfontein

For a vehicle based in Bloemfontein or the Free State, start with the local team. Tell us the year, make, model, engine, transmission and your town or suburb, plus any existing modifications and what you would like to improve.

Use the Boostech Bloemfontein vehicle enquiry form for a local recommendation. You can also read Namibia’s view of the international network and the Western Cape network guide.

title: Ford Ranger tuning, exhausts & downpipes
summary: Vehicle-specific development across the Ranger range, from the 2.0 single-turbo to the V6 Raptor.
image_alt: Ford Ranger 2.0 Bi-Turbo Stage 1 tuning by Boostech
body:
The developed range

From workhorse to Raptor

The breadth of the Ranger range is exactly why experience matters. These applications share a badge, but not one engine, one turbo system or one calibration strategy.

01ECU
calibration
02Automatic
calibration
03Developed

The Ford Ranger is not one vehicle with one tuning file. The range spans different generations, engine families, turbo layouts, transmissions and performance levels—from the hard-working 2.0 single-turbo to the Bi-Turbo Wildtrak, 2.3T petrol, 3.0 V6 and the range-topping Raptor.

Boostech’s development reflects those differences. We have worked across the Ranger range to produce vehicle-specific ECU calibrations, automatic-transmission solutions and supporting exhaust hardware. The objective is usable torque, better response and a powertrain that works as a complete system.

Development across the Ranger range

Each Ranger responds differently. A 2.0 single-turbo used daily or for commercial work needs a different torque strategy from a 2.0 Bi-Turbo Wildtrak, while the 3.0 V6 Ranger and Raptor require their own careful approach to boost, torque control, fuelling and gearbox coordination.

Our Stage 1 calibrations focus on the area drivers use most: low- and mid-range torque, throttle response, overtaking performance and more decisive delivery under load. Where an automatic calibration is available and suitable, it is coordinated with the engine software rather than treating the gearbox as an afterthought.

Ranger 2.0 single-turbo125 kW · 405 Nm → 145 kW · 480 NmNext-generation application
Ranger 2.0 Bi-Turbo153 kW · 506 Nm → 185 kW · 586 NmStage 1 development
Wildtrak / Raptor 2.0 Bi-Turbo157 kW · 500 Nm → 185 kW · 585 NmEngine and automatic calibration
Ranger 3.0 V6 TDCi184 kW · 591 Nm → 220 kW · 678 NmStage 1 development
Ranger Raptor 3.0 V6292 kW · 583 Nm → 325 kW · 740 NmSafe calibration on stock boost
Ranger 2.3T petrol222 kW · 452 Nm → 235 kW · 510 NmStage 1 remap
Earlier Ranger 2.0 single-turbo132 kW · 420 Nm → 150 kW · 500 NmStage 1 development

These are representative development figures, not a blanket promise for every vehicle. Exact output depends on the model year, ECU and software version, fuel, transmission, hardware and mechanical condition of the individual Ranger.

The important point

A Ford Ranger should feel stronger because the engine, turbo system, torque model and gearbox are working together—not because one number has been pushed as high as possible.

More than peak power

The way torque arrives matters as much as the maximum figure. A well-developed Ranger calibration should make towing easier, reduce unnecessary gearbox hunting, improve overtaking response and give the driver finer control in sand, on gravel and in everyday traffic.

  • Stronger, cleaner low- and mid-range torque
  • Sharper response without abrupt throttle behaviour
  • Engine and automatic calibration coordinated where available
  • Speed-limiter adjustment for selected applications
  • Automatic stop/start deactivation for supported models
  • EGR-related solutions where appropriate and legally permitted

Developed hardware

Exhausts and downpipes designed for the Ranger

Software works best when the supporting hardware is properly designed. We have developed Ranger downpipes and complete exhaust systems around the actual vehicle layout—not simply added a universal length of pipe. Fitment, clearance, flange alignment, flex sections, hangers, silencer choice and flow all matter.

A freer-flowing system can reduce unnecessary restriction and support stronger response, but bigger is not automatically better. The system must suit the engine, turbo layout, intended power level and how the vehicle is used. A daily-driven Ranger, a towing vehicle and a performance-focused Raptor do not necessarily need the same hardware or sound level.

Our downpipe development includes applications for the 2.0-litre Ranger range as well as the 3.0 V6 platforms. Complete systems are available for selected models, with calibration matched to the hardware when a Stage 2 package is appropriate.

Material and construction vary by application. T304 stainless steel is used on selected systems only; we will confirm the exact specification for your Ranger before quoting.

title: 2026 Isuzu D-Max 1.9 Ddi remapping
summary: New engine management, established calibration experience and the development behind the latest 1.9 Ddi.
body:

The resultSharper responseStronger mid-range

Boostech has been remapping the Isuzu 1.9 Ddi for years. It remains one of the most rewarding engines to calibrate, responding exceptionally well when boost, fuelling, torque control and throttle behaviour are developed as one coordinated package. The 2026 model continues that potential—but reaching it required new work.

The engine is familiar. The management is not.

The 2026 D-Max still carries the RZ4E 1.9-litre turbo-diesel name, but Isuzu has introduced its latest-generation engine-management system alongside significant hardware changes. Much like the newest Toyota platforms, this is not a case of loading an old calibration into a new vehicle. The ECU identification, software structure and access method have all moved forward.

Boostech is one of the first tuning companies able to work with this new generation. At the time access was achieved, complete supporting information was still being documented by parts of the tool-development industry. That is how far ahead the Boostech network has been working.

Leading the pack

When a new vehicle arrives, we do not wait for the market to tell us what is possible. Our network works together to establish access, understand the control strategy and develop the right solution.

What Isuzu changed for 2026

The updated 1.9 Ddi uses an electronically controlled turbo actuator in place of the previous vacuum actuator. This allows faster and more precise boost control. Isuzu also introduced a new high-pressure fuel pump and common-rail injection system, a redesigned combustion chamber, revised ECM calibration and faster-heating ceramic glow plugs.

Peak factory output remains 110 kW and 350 Nm, but the full 350 Nm is now available from 1,600 to 2,600 rpm. Isuzu says the revised engine produces 130 Nm more torque at 1,600 rpm than the outgoing version, giving the new D-Max noticeably stronger response before any remap is applied.

  • Electronically controlled turbo actuator
  • New high-pressure fuel pump and common rail
  • Redesigned combustion chamber
  • Latest-generation ECM calibration and data strategy
  • Ceramic glow plugs for faster cold starts
  • Full 350 Nm available from 1,600 rpm

Why years of 1.9 Ddi experience matter

New ECU access does not replace calibration experience. It only opens the door. Boostech already understands how the RZ4E responds under load, where useful torque should be delivered, how the automatic gearbox reacts and why smooth control is more important than one impressive peak number.

Our established 1.9 Ddi package lifts output from 110 kW and 350 Nm to approximately 150 kW and 450 Nm. More importantly, it transforms throttle response, low-speed pull, overtaking performance and everyday drivability while keeping a progressive, factory-like delivery.

With the 2026 Toyota Hilux N90, Boostech is not waiting for the local market to catch up. Development, testing and real-world tuning are already taking place across our international network.

One network. More experience.

Boostech Bloemfontein is connected to an established international network of tuning partners. Knowledge and feedback are shared across markets including Australia, South Africa and Europe, where vehicles operate under very different loads, climates and driving conditions.

That international reach matters most when a completely new vehicle arrives in Bloemfontein. Instead of using a local customer's Hilux as the starting point, we can draw on work already completed elsewhere in the network. The result is faster access to established solutions and a much broader base of real-world experience.

The Boostech difference

International development means we are not starting from zero when your new Hilux arrives at our workshop.

The Australian Stage 2 build

The featured N90 was completed by Boostech Australia and received the full Stage 2 treatment. It is a practical demonstration of what becomes possible when the ECU calibration, airflow, exhaust flow and gearbox behaviour are developed as one coordinated package.

That translates into the differences a driver actually uses: more decisive overtaking, stronger towing performance, improved throttle response and a Hilux that feels less restricted in everyday driving. Depending on vehicle condition, use and driving style, the additional torque and improved efficiency may also support better fuel consumption.

title: VW Amarok 3.0 V6: Beast Mode tuning
summary: How coordinated engine and gearbox calibration brings out the new Amarok V6’s potential.
image_alt: VW Amarok 3.0 V6 Beast Mode tuning advert
body:
01Improved power
and torque
02Reduced
turbo lag
03Sharper throttle
response
04Smoother
delivery

The new-generation Amarok 3.0 V6 is not simply a larger version of the 2.0 BiTurbo. It uses a different V6 engine architecture, a single variable-geometry turbocharger and a powertrain designed to deliver substantial torque across a broad operating range.

A different V6 platform

That distinction matters when the vehicle is calibrated. A larger engine does not automatically need aggressive boost or harsh torque delivery to feel strong. The V6 gives us the opportunity to improve response and mid-range performance while keeping the way the vehicle delivers its power smooth and predictable.

The variable-geometry turbocharger changes its effective turbine geometry according to engine speed and load. This helps the Amarok respond at lower engine speeds while still flowing effectively higher in the rev range. A professional calibration works with that system by coordinating boost control, fuelling, torque requests and protection strategies instead of simply asking for the largest possible peak number.

The objective

Wake up the V6 without taking away the refinement that makes the new Amarok such a capable long-distance, towing and everyday vehicle.

What changes behind the wheel?

The most useful difference is felt in the way the Amarok responds. Throttle inputs produce a more decisive reaction, torque arrives sooner and acceleration is stronger when overtaking, joining traffic or pulling a load. The engine feels less restrained without becoming difficult to drive smoothly.

  • Improved power and torque throughout the usable rev range
  • Reduced hesitation and turbo lag
  • Sharper throttle response
  • Stronger mid-range acceleration
  • More confident towing and load carrying
  • Smoother, more coordinated power delivery

Working with the automatic gearbox

Good engine calibration is about more than the engine alone. The gearbox responds to the torque information and requests exchanged across the powertrain. By keeping those torque models accurate and delivering the additional performance progressively, the vehicle can feel more settled and decisive instead of harsh or confused.

Depending on the exact model, software version and intended use, speed-limiter adjustment and automatic stop/start deactivation can also be discussed. These are optional changes, not assumptions built into every calibration.

Exhaust and emissions hardware

Understanding the DPF

The diesel particulate filter captures soot before it leaves the exhaust. In normal operation the vehicle periodically regenerates the filter by raising exhaust temperature and burning the collected material. Short trips, unsuitable operating conditions, sensor faults or an underlying engine problem can prevent successful regeneration and eventually cause restriction, warning lights or reduced-power operation.

DPF removal is a separate mechanical and software procedure, not an automatic part of a performance remap. On an appropriate application it can reduce exhaust restriction and eliminate repeated filter-related downtime, but the decision must account for the vehicle’s use, condition, warranty position and the requirements that apply where it is registered and operated.

Before recommending any solution, the vehicle should be assessed properly. A failed sensor, boost leak, injector problem or another engine fault should not be disguised by software. The correct solution begins with understanding why the system is giving trouble.

title: GWM P-Series 2.0 TD Stage 1 remap
summary: Low-down torque, throttle response and the eight-speed automatic, with exhaust development examples.

The GWM P-Series has established itself as a serious contender in the Southern African bakkie market. Its comfortable interior, capable 2.0-litre turbo-diesel engine and smooth eight-speed ZF automatic gearbox make it an excellent platform for professional ECU remapping.

Stronger performance where it matters

In standard form, the P-Series can feel hesitant at lower engine speeds, particularly when pulling away, overtaking, towing or carrying additional weight. Our Stage 1 calibration improves torque delivery, throttle response and turbo behaviour, giving the vehicle a more decisive response without making it harsh or difficult to drive smoothly.

  • Stronger low-down torque
  • Substantially reduced turbo lag
  • Improved throttle response and mid-range acceleration
  • Easier overtaking, towing and load carrying
  • Smoother everyday drivability
More than a peak number.

The biggest improvement is how readily the P-Series responds and how confidently it carries its torque through everyday driving.

Working with the eight-speed ZF gearbox

One of the strengths of the GWM P-Series is its eight-speed ZF automatic gearbox. With the correct engine and automatic gearbox calibration, the additional torque works with the transmission instead of fighting against it.

Gear changes remain fast and smooth while the vehicle responds more confidently when acceleration is requested. Improved torque delivery can also reduce unnecessary hunting between gears when towing, carrying a load or driving on inclines. The result is a more coordinated powertrain—not merely a larger peak figure.

Calibrated for the individual vehicle

A Boostech remap is selected and prepared for the exact vehicle, ECU software, gearbox, existing hardware and intended use. Existing boost leaks, turbo problems, injector faults, warning lights or gearbox issues should be resolved before additional performance is requested.

Our priority is strong, clean and predictable performance within sensible operating limits. Actual results may differ slightly according to model year, ECU version, fuel quality, vehicle condition and installed hardware.

title: Do we tune Audi, BMW and sedans?
summary: Passenger cars are part of the Boostech story too. Find out what determines compatibility.
body:
The short answer: yes.From an everyday diesel sedan to a turbo-petrol performance car, we first identify the exact ECU and then confirm the correct tuning route.

Because Boostech is well known for Hilux, Ranger, Land Cruiser and other bakkie tuning, customers often assume that is all we do. It isn't. Passenger-vehicle ECU remapping has always formed part of our work.

What can a passenger-car remap improve?

The objective depends on the vehicle and the way you use it. A sensible calibration can improve throttle response, low- and mid-range torque, overtaking performance and overall drivability. Turbocharged petrol and diesel engines usually offer the most noticeable gains, although selected naturally aspirated vehicles may also have useful calibration options.

  • Stronger power and torque
  • Sharper throttle response
  • Smoother, more usable power delivery
  • Improved overtaking performance
  • Potential efficiency improvement when driven sensibly
The badge is only the starting point.

“It's a BMW” or “it's an Audi” is not enough information. The model year, engine, ECU, software version and vehicle condition determine what can actually be done.

Does every model support the same options?

No. Even two visually identical vehicles can use different control units or software. Some newer ECUs are locked, some require bench access or an unlock procedure, and certain engines or gearboxes need additional checks before tuning. Available functions also change as professional tool manufacturers release new protocols.

That is why we confirm compatibility against the exact vehicle instead of making a blanket promise based only on the manufacturer.

What should you send us?

To answer quickly and accurately, send the make, exact model, model year, engine size, fuel type and current power output if known. A clear photo of the licence disc or VIN is often the fastest way to avoid confusion between similar versions.

title: What makes 1-Exhaust different?
summary: Vehicle-specific downpipes, materials, fitment and the thinking behind a complete exhaust system.
image_alt: 1-Exhaust Toyota Hilux GD-6 system with vehicle-specific downpipe
body:
01Vehicle-specific
engineering
02Surge-preventing
downpipes
03T304 stainless
construction
04Direct bolt-on
fitment

A performance exhaust should not be judged only by pipe diameter or how loud it sounds. The best system is the one that manages gas flow correctly, fits the vehicle properly and supports the engine and turbocharger without introducing new problems.

The system matters as a whole

Exhaust flow is affected by every transition, bend, flange, joint, silencer and change in diameter. Making one section extremely large while ignoring the rest of the system can create turbulence, poor fitment, leaks, unwanted resonance or unstable boost behaviour. That is why 1-Exhaust systems are developed for specific vehicles rather than treated as universal lengths of pipe.

Pipe diameter is selected for the engine, turbocharger and intended performance level. Routing follows the available space beneath the vehicle while maintaining clearance from the body, drivetrain, heat-sensitive components and suspension movement. Mounting points are positioned to support the system correctly instead of forcing it into place during fitment.

The 1-Exhaust principle

More flow is valuable only when it remains controlled. A proper system improves breathing without sacrificing fitment, stability or everyday usability.

Downpipes engineered to prevent surging

The downpipe is the first major section of exhaust after the turbocharger, and it has a disproportionate effect on how smoothly exhaust gas expands and leaves the turbine. It cannot be designed as a crude oversized tube with an abrupt transition at the turbo outlet.

Poorly designed high-flow downpipes can disturb pressure behaviour and boost control, producing oscillation that the driver experiences as surging. The 1-Exhaust approach controls the outlet diameter, expansion, transitions, bends and overall routing to promote stable flow. Correct sensor positions and properly formed connections allow the engine-management system to receive consistent information and control boost predictably.

In practical terms, the downpipe is engineered not only to reduce unnecessary restriction, but also to prevent surging. That is a crucial difference between a purpose-built performance component and a generic pipe fabricated only to fit between two points.

Materials and fabrication

Automotive-grade T304 stainless steel tubing and silencers are used on applicable 1-Exhaust performance systems for exceptional durability, corrosion resistance and long-term performance. But the quality goes far beyond the stainless steel itself: every bracket is precision laser-cut and every hanger is individually turned on a lathe, rather than relying on generic mass-produced components.

Together with clean TIG-welded joints and thick flanges designed to resist warping through repeated heating and cooling cycles, this attention to detail delivers exceptional fitment, strength and consistency—making 1-Exhaust quality a cut above almost anything else on the market.

  • T304 stainless steel on applicable performance systems
  • TIG-welded joints
  • Every bracket precision laser-cut
  • Every hanger individually turned on a lathe
  • Thick flanges designed to resist warping
  • Correct hanger, sensor and connection locations
  • Vehicle-specific routing and direct bolt-on fitment

Why fitment quality matters

A correctly engineered bolt-on system should line up with the vehicle’s mounting points and connections without being pulled, twisted or forced into position. This reduces strain on flanges, hangers and surrounding components while helping the system maintain consistent clearances under acceleration, braking and chassis movement.

Professional fitment still matters. Connections must be sealed, hangers aligned and clearances checked with the vehicle on the lift and again once the system has completed its first heat cycle. Ask Boostech Bloemfontein to confirm local supply and fitment arrangements, including the correct hardware and leak checks.

Designed around the application

Not one system for every vehicle

The correct exhaust for a Hilux GD-6 is not automatically the correct answer for a Land Cruiser V8, Ford Ranger Bi-Turbo or Ranger Raptor. Turbo layout, engine output, available space, body style, wheelbase and intended use all influence the final configuration.

That is why Boostech confirms the exact model, engine, cab or body style and existing modifications before ordering. The aim is to supply the correct system the first time—not modify a nearly suitable system until it fits.

Explore available 1-Exhaust systems →

Exhaust hardware and ECU calibration

A freer-flowing exhaust can improve response and reduce restriction on its own, but the best combined result comes when the ECU calibration is written for the installed hardware. The software can then coordinate boost, torque request and fuelling around the improved flow rather than relying on the ECU to adapt around an unknown modification.

This is particularly important on modern turbo-diesels. Boostech does not use an exhaust as an excuse for excessive boost, overfuelling or smoke. The objective is stronger usable performance, predictable exhaust temperatures and smooth delivery in the conditions the vehicle actually works in.

Sound without sacrificing usability

A deeper and more purposeful exhaust note is part of the appeal, but louder is not always better. Pipe size, silencer configuration, vehicle body and the presence of a downpipe all affect the final sound. Customers can discuss whether they want a refined touring note, something sportier or a more aggressive result before the system is ordered.

title: Do we dyno every vehicle?
summary: The difference between developing a calibration and installing it, and where dyno testing adds value.
image_alt: Pickup developed for the open road with a workshop dyno shown in the background
body:
01Proven
calibrations
02Real-world
development
03Responsible
engine limits
04Dyno testing
when required

A dynamometer is extremely useful when it has a genuine development, measurement or diagnostic purpose. But placing every standard vehicle on rollers does not automatically improve an already proven remap.

Development is different from installation

When a new engine, ECU or vehicle platform is developed, proper testing is required. This can include controlled data logging, repeated calibration revisions, road testing and, where appropriate, dyno testing.

Once a calibration has been properly developed, tested and refined across multiple vehicles, that work does not disappear. Installing the proven calibration on another mechanically healthy vehicle with the same engine and ECU is not the same as beginning development again.

Boostech has many years of tuning experience and operates as part of a wider dealer and development network. We do not treat every Hilux, Ranger, Fortuner or Land Cruiser as an entirely new experiment.

Our development philosophy

We develop vehicles for the open road—because that is where our customers actually drive them.

Developed where the vehicle actually works

A vehicle does not spend its life strapped to rollers. On the road it must deal with gradients, overtaking, part-throttle acceleration, changing gears, natural airflow, different engine loads, altitude, ambient temperature, cruising and stop-start driving.

These conditions reveal whether torque arrives smoothly, the gearbox behaves correctly and the vehicle remains responsive and predictable in everyday use. Peak power at full throttle is only one part of a successful calibration. Boost control, fuel pressure, torque delivery, throttle response, cruising efficiency and drivability matter just as much.

What does a dyno actually do?

A dyno allows a stationary vehicle to be operated under controlled load and measures power and torque at the wheels. It is particularly valuable when developing a new platform, testing a heavily modified vehicle, creating a custom calibration, diagnosing a fault or obtaining a measured before-and-after result.

It remains a tool—not a guarantee of quality. A poor or overly aggressive calibration can still produce an impressive graph, while the graph may say very little about towing behaviour, part-throttle response, gearbox calibration or long-distance reliability.

The additional stress of a dyno run

During a power run, the engine and drivetrain are taken through a sustained high-load acceleration while the vehicle remains stationary. Repeated full-load runs place demand on the engine, turbocharger, cooling system, gearbox or clutch, transfer case, differentials, driveshafts and tyres.

On the road, airflow through the radiator, intercooler, underbody and engine bay increases naturally with vehicle speed. On a dyno, powerful workshop fans must reproduce as much of that airflow as possible. If cooling provision is inadequate, heat can build rapidly around the intake, cooling system, transmission and exhaust.

The tyres also run against rollers under high load while the vehicle is secured in place, generating heat and forces different from ordinary road operation. A properly equipped dyno in experienced hands manages these factors, so dyno testing is not inherently unsafe. It is nevertheless a demanding test and should have a clear purpose.

There is little benefit in repeatedly subjecting a standard customer vehicle to full-load runs merely to demonstrate an established calibration again. If the run provides meaningful diagnostic or measurement data, it makes sense. If it is only for marketing theatre, the extra mechanical stress, time and cost achieve very little for the customer.

Why we do not dyno every standard vehicle

Our established calibrations have already undergone the necessary development. We understand the sensible operating limits of the engines and drivetrains we work with and stay within proven parameters.

More importantly, customers should not be used as test subjects while someone attempts to understand their vehicle for the first time.

Every vehicle still needs to be healthy

Vehicles of the same model can respond slightly differently because of mileage, maintenance, fuel quality, altitude, temperature, tyre size, carbon buildup and the condition of the turbocharger, injectors, sensors and intake system.

A remap cannot repair a worn turbo, blocked filter, leaking boost pipe or faulty sensor. If a vehicle behaves unexpectedly, has extensive modifications or requires something beyond our established specification, further diagnosis, logging or dyno testing may be recommended.

What about advertised power figures?

Our advertised figures represent the tested and proven output expected from that engine and calibration. They are not a promise that every individual vehicle will produce precisely the same number in every set of conditions.

If a customer requires a measured before-and-after result for their particular vehicle, individual dyno testing can be arranged where available. That is a measurement service—it does not mean the calibration must be developed again from the beginning.

title: Toyota Quantum: understanding the factory speed limiter
summary: How software limiter adjustment works on selected models, and why vehicle use and legal limits matter.
body:
Common factory limiter100km/h
→
Selected adjustment120km/h
HardwareSoftwareNo add-on box

Many Toyota Quantums are supplied with a factory speed limiter set to 100 km/h. That may suit certain commercial applications, but it can feel unnecessarily restrictive when the vehicle is privately used or spends substantial time on the open road.

Why does the Quantum stop accelerating?

When the vehicle reaches its programmed limit, the ECU restricts further acceleration even when the engine still has sufficient power available. This is an electronic control strategy rather than a sign that the engine has reached its natural performance limit.

The limitation can be particularly noticeable on long-distance journeys, when descending, or when the driver begins an overtaking manoeuvre expecting the vehicle to continue accelerating. A limiter adjustment does not create extra engine power, but it prevents the original 100 km/h setting from becoming the artificial ceiling.

Important distinction

Adjusting the limiter changes the vehicle’s electronic ceiling. It does not change the posted speed limit, the driver’s legal obligations or the distance required to overtake safely.

Adjustment to 120 km/h

On selected Toyota Quantum models, Boostech Performance Engineering can recalibrate the factory limiter from 100 km/h to 120 km/h. The work is completed through the vehicle’s software, without an unnecessary external speed module or add-on box.

  • Common factory limiter: 100 km/h
  • Selected adjusted limiter: 120 km/h
  • Software-based calibration
  • No unnecessary hardware changes
  • Suitable for selected private and long-distance applications

Eligibility depends on the exact model year, ECU, software version and how the vehicle is registered and used. We confirm these details before recommending or carrying out the adjustment.

Overtaking still requires judgement

Reaching a factory limiter during an overtaking manoeuvre can be unexpected, but raising the limiter should never be treated as permission to make a marginal pass. The driver must still allow adequate visibility, distance and time, remain within the applicable speed limit and account for the Quantum’s load, braking distance and road conditions.

The benefit is flexibility: where 120 km/h is legally permitted and appropriate for that particular vehicle, the driver is no longer unexpectedly held at the original 100 km/h electronic ceiling.

Road limits and vehicle classification matter

A 120 km/h limiter setting does not make 120 km/h legal everywhere in Bloemfontein or South Africa. Posted limits always apply, and lower limits may apply according to the road, conditions, vehicle classification, passenger or commercial use, permits and other legal requirements.

The driver and vehicle operator remain responsible for complying with all applicable laws. A limiter adjustment does not alter the vehicle’s registration category or remove any operating restrictions attached to its use.

A brand ambassador should do more than display a logo. Armand Basson uses his vehicles in some of Southern Africa's most remote and demanding environments. That makes his long-term experience with Boostech valuable: it is genuine, hard-earned and tested in the real world.

Proof measured in kilometres

Armand is one of Namibia's most experienced off-road drivers. He regularly travels through remote terrain, frequently with heavy loads and far from the easy support of a city workshop. In that environment, usable torque, predictable gearbox behaviour and durability matter much more than a headline number.

His Toyota 2.8 GD-6 automatic has run a Boostech Stage 2 calibration, gearbox adaptation and straight-pipe setup since day one. After nearly 70,000 km in just over a year, the combination has continued to deliver the strong, responsive and enjoyable drive he wanted.

In Armand's words

“My Land Cruiser 2.8 auto—what a pleasure. Nearly 70,000 km in just over a year. I love this Cruiser. Runs like the wind!”

Why Armand is an outstanding ambassador

Armand understands what a vehicle must do when conditions are unforgiving. He can feel the difference between aggressive calibration and useful performance, and he values the same qualities we engineer for: torque where it is needed, clean drivability, a coordinated powertrain and confidence over distance.

That honesty is exactly why we are proud to have him as a Boostech brand ambassador. His feedback is informed by decades behind the wheel and by kilometres covered where vehicles must work properly.

title: Boostech Namibia, Springbok and Cape Town
summary: A regional story from Boostech Namibia, showing how the network supports customers across borders.

context: This regional report comes from Boostech Namibia. It describes that branch’s Springbok visits and the Western Cape operation. For Bloemfontein enquiries, contact Pieter using the links below.

Namibia remains our home, but the vehicles we support—and the relationships behind them—do not stop at the border. Boostech Namibia has been visiting Springbok in the Northern Cape regularly, while our established Western Cape operation gives customers a permanent Boostech presence in Cape Town.

Regular visits to Springbok

Springbok is an important link between Namibia and South Africa. It is close enough to serve Namibian customers travelling south, but it is also home to bakkies and working vehicles that face the same long distances, heavy loads, heat and overtaking demands we understand so well.

Our visits are planned around customer demand and give Northern Cape owners access to professional ECU remapping, vehicle assessment and selected performance solutions without having to travel all the way to Cape Town. These are not once-off appearances: Springbok has become a regular part of the area we serve.

Regional support that is real

A network only matters when it works in practice. Regular Springbok visits and a permanent Cape Town base allow us to support customers before, during and after the work is completed.

A permanent Boostech presence in Cape Town

Boostech is also firmly established in the Western Cape. Through Boostech Western Cape, customers in Cape Town and the surrounding areas have direct access to the same performance-engineering approach, proven calibration knowledge and wider Boostech development network.

The Cape Town operation is based in the northern suburbs and serves Durbanville, Brackenfell and the wider Western Cape. It provides ECU remapping, mobile vehicle tuning and access to properly engineered performance exhaust solutions. For full details, supported services and Cape Town enquiries, visit boostechwc.com.

Why the connection matters to Namibian customers

Many Namibians travel to the Western Cape for business, holidays, vehicle purchases or specialist work. Having Boostech on both sides of that journey means our customers are not dealing with an unknown workshop if they need advice or support while in South Africa.

  • Regular Boostech service visits to Springbok
  • Permanent support in Cape Town and the northern suburbs
  • Shared calibration knowledge across the Boostech network
  • Vehicle-specific ECU remapping and diagnostics
  • Performance exhaust supply and fitment options
  • Continuity for customers travelling between Namibia and South Africa
